newsitem.title: USA: H.F.Ahmanson amends Great Western suit.
newsitem.headline: H.F.Ahmanson amends Great Western suit.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co Friday said it filed an amendment to its lawsuit against Great Western Financial Friday related to Washington Mutual Savings Bank's attempt to account for the acquisition of Great Western as a pooling of interests.
In a statement, Ahmanson asked the Delaware Chancery Court to disclose the risks of not being able to pool on its ability to complete the transaction.
Ahmanson recently raised its hostile bid for Great Western to $6.68 billion, topping Wahington Mutual's friendly offer of $6.44 billion.

Ahmanson said on December 19, 1996, Great Western made certain modifications to its stock compensation and benefit plans for officers, directors and senior executives that changed the equity interest of the voting stock, including changing the definition of a change of control for the purpose of triggering the acceleration of vesting of stock options.

Ahmanson said also, during 1996, Great Western granted approximately 3,750,000 stock options to its officers, directors and senior executives -- an 833 percent increase over the number of options granted in 1995.

Under accepted accounting practice, these changes in equity interests by Great Western are presumed to have been made in contemplation of the Washington Mutual merger, Ahmanson said, adding evidence that Great Western was contemplating a possible combination with any party at the time these plans were adopted could preclude pooling.
